facts.text: Bobtown developed as a small rural community during the eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries, tied to the agricultural economy of northern Accomack County.
Local records from the late nineteenth century mention Bobtown in the Peninsula Enterprise newspaper between 1883 and 1895 regarding regional events.
Several homes along Bobtown Road dating to the early 1900s exemplify the frame construction typical of rural Eastern Shore architecture.
The Great Depression hit Bobtown's rural economy hard, causing potato prices to collapse and leading to farm foreclosures by 1934.
World War Two revitalized agriculture in Bobtown, turning the region into a key supplier of vegetables and poultry for national needs.
Bobtown sits within a low-lying coastal landscape at an elevation of approximately thirteen to twenty-three feet above sea level.
